short: His unfinished epic, the Aeneid, became Rome's national foundation myth.
full:
Publius Vergilius Maro was born near Mantua in 70 BC and spent much of his career under Augustus's patronage, encouraged by Maecenas. His pastoral Eclogues and didactic Georgics established him as the leading poet of the age before he began the Aeneid, an epic tracing the Trojan Aeneas's flight to Italy and the mythical origins of Rome, deliberately answering Homer while casting Augustus as the culmination of a divinely sanctioned destiny.

Virgil died in 19 BC, having asked that the unfinished manuscript be burned; Augustus overruled him and had it published with only minor editing. The Aeneid was almost immediately adopted as a school text and the closest thing Rome had to a national scripture, read for its Latin, its politics and its vision of Roman mission for the rest of antiquity and long after.
